title: Beyond the Numbers: How Ghana's 2026 Mid-Year Budget Is Quietly Rewiring a Culture of Impunity

detail.title: Beyond the Numbers: How Ghana's 2026 Mid-Year Budget Is Quietly Rewiring a Culture of Impunity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial, professional, political, or personal interest whether direct or indirect in the individuals, institutions, or cases discussed in this paper, including the Ministry of Finance of Ghana, the Ghana Revenue Authority, GoldBod, or any party named or referenced in ongoing legal proceedings mentioned herein. No competing interests are declared.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper is a policy analysis and opinion-based commentary drawing exclusively on publicly available information — official government budget statements, Parliamentary proceedings, and public news reporting. It does not involve human or animal subjects, primary data collection, surveys, interviews, or experimentation, and therefore did not require ethics committee or Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval.

detail.abstract: Ghana’s 2026 Mid-Year Budget Review, presented to Parliament on July 23, 2026, has been read primarily as a macroeconomic document, one confirming disinflation to 5.3 percent, a 12.3 percent rise in domestic revenue, and an imminent exit from the IMF’s Extended Credit Facility programme. This paper argues that the more consequential story lies outside the headline indicators, in a parallel set of enforcement reforms that together constitute an attempt to restructure the incentive environment around public and private financial crime in Ghana. Drawing on the budget statement and contemporaneous reporting on procurement reform, high-profile prosecutions, transnational cyber-fraud enforcement, and the crackdown on illegal small-scale mining (galamsey) and gold laundering, the paper develops a single argument: a substantial share of the liquidity that has historically circulated in the Ghanaian economy through inflated public contracts, romance-scam and wire-fraud proceeds, and untraceable gold exports, was never sustainable, since it depended on informality, weak enforcement, and the absence of cross-border accountability. The current budget’s combination of procurement tightening, active prosecution, and cooperation on extradition should therefore be understood not merely as fiscal austerity but as a deliberate attempt to convert unstable, criminogenic liquidity into narrower but durable, taxable, and legitimate revenue. The paper considers both the promise and the limits of this approach, and proposes that its ultimate test is durability beyond the current political and media cycle.

title: K-waves of Global GDP per Capita with a 2-year Lag (1966–2021) And Large Cycles of Solar Activity Extremes (1964–2019): R = -0.796, Forecast to 2037
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: K-waves of Global GDP per Capita with a 2-year Lag (1966–2021) And Large Cycles of Solar Activity Extremes (1964–2019): R = -0.796, Forecast to 2037
detail.abstract:
This preprint uses a methodological approach developed by W. S. Jevons and A. L. Chizhevsky. Over the study period, Wolf numbers in years of solar activity extremes were compared with annual growth rates of global per capita GDP with a lag of two years. The correlation coefficient was -0.796, and statistical significance was p = 0.0037.

The main limitation of the theories of N. D. Kondratiev, J. A. Schumpeter, and S. Yu. Glazyev is that they fail to explain the underlying cause of cyclicality. They described in detail how capital is renewed, how innovations are introduced, and how technological paradigms change. However, a key question remains open: why do billions of independent people around the world begin to innovate in cycles rather than chaotically?

My theory eliminates this limitation. K-cycles of innovation are merely a consequence. The root cause lies elsewhere. It is the Sun, with its cycles of activity, that acts as the unified cosmic orchestrator: it strongly influences the efficiency of the brain and the effectiveness of innovation, thereby setting the overall K-cycle for the global macroeconomy.

With the Wolf number in 2024 (the year of maximum solar activity) equal to 154.7, the growth of global GDP per capita in 2026 will be 1.35%.

With a predicted Wolf number of 156.02 for 2035 (the year of the next solar maximum), global GDP per capita growth in 2037 will be 1.30%. This makes it possible to forecast K-waves in the global economic situation based on solar activity forecasts.

title: Systematic Integration of Systemic Risk Management and Multi-factor Pricing Dynamics in S&P 500 Price Discovery

detail.title: Systematic Integration of Systemic Risk Management and Multi-factor Pricing Dynamics in S&P 500 Price Discovery
detail.abstract:
The modern financial landscape is defined by the rapid assimilation of diverse data streams into asset prices, a process known as price discovery. At the epicenter of this mechanism is the S&P 500 index, which serves as the primary benchmark for global equity risk. Traditionally, price discovery research focused on the lead-lag relationship between the cash market and the futures market. However, the proliferation of complex derivatives, high-frequency trading, and the elevation of volatility as a distinct asset class have rendered these classical views insufficient. A contemporary understanding of price discovery requires an integrated framework that acknowledges the forward-looking information embedded in the VIX microstructure and the systematic risk premiums captured by multi-factor models.

The relationship between the S&P 500 and its volatility gauge, the VIX, has evolved from a simple contemporaneous negative correlation—the "leverage effect"—to a sophisticated interdependency where the VIX microstructure informs the future trajectory of equity returns. Concurrently, the academic consensus has shifted toward a more granular decomposition of returns, incorporating factors that go beyond the market beta. Specifically, the integration of profitability signals, macroeconomic indicators, the futures-cash basis, and market microstructure frictions provides a robust lens through which the impounding of information can be analyzed. This report investigates this integration, proposes a new "Information Convergence Price Discovery Theory" (ICPDT), and outlines an academic path for validating these complex interactions in the world’s most liquid equity market.

detail.abstract: The article examines the climate strategy of Rosneft PJSC through the prism of corporate risk management, conceptualizing it as a comprehensive, multi-tiered framework for the identification, classification, quantitative and qualitative assessment, and subsequent mitigation of climate risks that exert direct and indirect influence on the company's financial stability, operational efficiency, investment appeal, and long-term strategic viability. The analysis is grounded in a fundamental premise of contemporary financial management theory: within the context of the global energy transition, climate factors are evolving from external externalities into endogenous determinants of business capitalization, necessitating systematic governance on par with traditional production and market risks. 1 The study identifies the principal sources of climate vulnerability, demonstrating that the formulation and execution of an adaptation strategy transcend mere corporate social responsibility or reputational maintenance, emerging instead as a critical determinant of sustained competitiveness in the medium and long term.

title: The Unitary Patent System: Lessons and Prospects for Africa
affiliations: Afe Babalola University

detail.title: The Unitary Patent System: Lessons and Prospects for Africa

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This is an undergraduate thesis made in partial fulfillment of the requirements of the award of the degree of Bachelor of Laws (LL.B) by Afe Babalola University, Ado-Ekiti, Ekiti State, Nigeria.

detail.abstract: Since the advent of patent protection, the territoriality of patent has threatened the effectiveness of patent protection globally. This issue has given rise to an innovative system known as the ‘Unitary Patent System’. This system is only operational under three jurisdictions worldwide, the Gulf Cooperation Council Patent Office, the European Union, and the Organisation Africaine de la Propriété Intellectuelle. This study focuses on the latter two. This study examine the existing patent systems in the European Union and the Organisation Africaine de la Propriété Intellectuelle and served a comparative analysis, focusing on the European trends that could be adopted by Organisation Africaine de la Propriété Intellectuelle and the possibility of unifying efforts across Africa. This study adopted the doctrinal research methodology to arrive at its postulations. This study found that, even though the Unitary Patent System is existent in Africa, only a small fraction of African states (particularly the participating member states of the OAPI which are all francophone states) benefit from this system. Also, this study found that though the system is functioning in Africa, there are still a couple of lacunae and shortcomings which need to be rectified. This study concluded that there is a need to concentrate on the reformation of the system as a whole through introduction of substantive examination, provision of additional incentives for innovation, reinforcing international cooperation, revisiting competence of national courts, as well as encouraging harmonising efforts between Intellectual Property Organisations regarding patent protection.

detail.title: The Unnecessary War Between Banks and Stablecoins A Curve-Gated Reserve Partnership Under the GENIUS Act

Sesame Vault serves stablecoin issuers commercially and would benefit from growth in the institutional stablecoin market and from adoption of the reserve structures discussed in this paper. It relies exclusively on publicly available sources, including Federal Reserve Economic Data, U.S. Treasury Fiscal Data, published issuer disclosures and attestations, regulatory rule text and public agency documents.

detail.abstract: The GENIUS Act makes stablecoins safer, but it leaves their business model tied to the shortest interest rates and channels a growing pool of reserve demand into Treasury bills. This paper proposes a way to address both weaknesses without relaxing reserve rules or allowing issuers to reach for duration. Under a curve-gated bank– issuer partnership, the issuer keeps an overnight, collateralized reserve asset while a supervised bank owns the term asset, hedge and associated capital and liquidity risk. The partnership activates only when expected maturity carry clears the bank’s costs, hurdle and conservative stress tests. The bank then shares a capped portion through the overnight repo rate; otherwise, the gate stays closed. This is risk-managed, episodic carry, not guaranteed yield or issuer-owned duration. The mechanism is designed to be especially useful in easing cycles and some low-rate environments, when front-end reserve income is under the greatest pressure and stablecoin issuers need diversification most, but curve steepness can still support shared carry. In eligible historical windows, the following quarter supported capped premiums averaging about 60 basis points. The proposal could make issuer economics more resilient, give banks a compensated channel for holding highquality liquid assets and broaden Treasury demand beyond bills, while preserving daily redemption liquidity and the holder’s non-yield-bearing claim. Exposure capped pilots under ordinary prudential treatment should test this alignment in practice.

detail.abstract: Nigeria is projected to become the third most populous country in the world by 2050, raising concerns about its capacity to provide adequate food for its rapidly growing population. This study examines Nigeria's ability to feed its population using the Malthusian Population Theory. The study adopts a qualitative research approach based on documentary analysis of secondary data obtained from scholarly journals, government publications, and reports of international organizations. Findings show that Nigeria possesses enormous agricultural potential capable of supporting its population. However, insecurity, poor infrastructure, climate change, weak agricultural mechanization, post-harvest losses, rapid urbanization, and ineffective policy implementation continue to limit agricultural productivity and food availability. The study argues that Nigeria's food security challenge is largely a problem of low productivity and poor governance rather than absolute scarcity of resources as suggested by Malthus. It concludes that increased investment in agricultural modernization, rural infrastructure, climate-smart farming, and effective policy implementation will enhance food production and ensure sustainable food security despite continued population growth.

title: Behavioural Attrition, Product Specificity, and the Conditional Case for Consumer Packaging Reuse
affiliations: Faculty of Environmental and Urban Change, York University

detail.title: Behavioural Attrition, Product Specificity, and the Conditional Case for Consumer Packaging Reuse
detail.abstract: Reusable consumer packaging is widely presented as an environmentally superior alternative to single-use formats, yet its performance is conditional rather than inherent. Reusable containers carry higher upfront material, energy, and infrastructure burdens that are repaid only through repeated cycles of use. This report introduces a diagnostic framework evaluating performance across three interconnected ledgers: a participation ledger tracking human engagement, a circulation ledger tracking container assets, and an outcome ledger measuring net single-use displacement and impact per delivered unit.  The core empirical finding identifies a severe willingness-likelihood gap. In a survey of 441 North American consumers across 22 product categories, mean stated support fell from 3.09 (willingness in principle) to 2.17 (self-assessed likelihood of use) to 1.66 (likelihood of engaging with a refill station) on five-point scales. Convenience barriers, convenience orientation, and hygiene concerns proved to be the strongest predictors of this decline. Small stage-level dropouts compound multiplicatively across the behavioral pathway—retaining 90% of participants across six independent stages leaves only 53% retention overall.  System performance is heavily bounded by product specificity (residue, hygiene, and purchase frequency) and system architecture. Operating case studies—including Germany’s refillable beverage market, Coca-Cola’s Latin American returnables, Loop, and France’s mandated fast-food tableware—demonstrate that reuse succeeds under dense routines with standardized, high-value assets, but fails when friction, costs, or container leakage override environmental break-even thresholds. Consequently, industry and policymakers must evaluate configurations longitudinally by achieved cycle performance and retention rather than relying on initial sign-ups or format counts.

title: Cost Analysis of the Spread Option
affiliations: McMaster University and University of Science and Technology of China

detail.title: Cost Analysis of the Spread Option
detail.abstract:
The classical Black–Scholes framework implies that the total cost of
obtaining ownership of an asset at maturity through a European call op-
tion, measured by the option premium plus the discounted exercise price,
is minimized when the strike price is zero. In this paper, we extend this
cost-based perspective to spread options. Using the LT-WKB approxi-
mation for spread option pricing under a Constant Elasticity of Variance
(CEV) model, we analyze the dependence of the total acquisition cost
on the strike parameter. Numerical experiments reveal that the minimum
totalcostisnotalwaysattainedatzerostrike. Forsuﬃcientlyhighcorrela-
tion between the underlying assets, long maturities, and certain elasticity
parameters, the cost function develops an interior minimum at a positive
strike. We provide an analytical characterization of this phenomenon by
deriving the derivative of the total cost with respect to the strike and
identifying the mechanism governing the transition from a boundary min-
imum to an interior minimum. In particular, we show that a suﬃciently
strong reduction in eﬀective volatility can dominate the direct exercise-
cost eﬀect, causing the total acquisition cost to decrease initially from zero
strike.

title: Dynamic Bargaining with Incomplete Information: Theory and Experimental Evidence
affiliations: City University of Hong Kong (CityU), , , Max Planck Institute for Behavioral Economics and

detail.title: Dynamic Bargaining with Incomplete Information: Theory and Experimental Evidence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The research described in this article was approved by the ethics committee of the University of Cologne.

detail.abstract: Private information is often viewed as a source of bargaining power. We argue that its value depends on how bargaining translates hidden values into prices. We study this link in a modelguided, continuous-time laboratory experiment with 384 subjects and 5,393 bilateral negotiations. The experiment varies information structure and transaction costs while preserving an unstructured bargaining protocol. Bargaining reveals private information only partially. Rather than separating through delay, subjects rapidly exchange offers and narrow the gap between opening positions through successive revisions. This partial revelation generates price compression: deal prices respond to private values, but less than full revelation predicts. Consequently, private information has different distributional effects across types. High-value informed buyers earn information rents, whereas intermediate types are harmed. In our setting, private information becomes bargaining power only when bargaining translates information into prices with sufficient precision.

detail.title: A Brief Review of Publications on the Azerbaijani Business Environment
detail.abstract: This paper provides a concise overview of Azerbaijan's recent socio-economic transformation, focusing on structural reforms, macroeconomic resilience, and future development priorities. It examines emerging trends in higher education, including the expansion of artificial intelligence, digital technologies, STEM disciplines, and university–industry collaboration, alongside the country's broader transition toward a diversified, innovation-driven economy. The report highlights reforms in digital governance, green energy, logistics, and the non-oil sector, while discussing persistent challenges such as inflation, limited non-oil foreign direct investment, and continued dependence on hydrocarbon revenues. Particular attention is given to Azerbaijan's macroeconomic framework, including the role of the State Oil Fund (SOFAZ), exchange rate management, resilience to external shocks, and the implications of Dutch disease for long-term competitiveness. The findings suggest that although Azerbaijan has strengthened its fiscal and external buffers and improved institutional capacity, sustained economic diversification, governance reforms, innovation, and productivity-enhancing policies remain essential to achieving the objectives of the Azerbaijan 2030 development strategy.

title: Regulatory Enforcement, Tax Penalties, and Fiscal Pressure: A Prisoner's Dilemma Analysis of Government Behavior in the Global Economic Recession
affiliations: Zhongnan University of Economics and Law

detail.title: Regulatory Enforcement, Tax Penalties, and Fiscal Pressure: A Prisoner's Dilemma Analysis of Government Behavior in the Global Economic Recession

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This study gratefully acknowledges Zhongnan University of Economics and Law (the author’s alma mater) for providing academic training and a solid research foundation, and thanks Bainian Cloud (Beijing) Cloud Computing Co., Ltd. and China Hi-Tech (Beijing) Technology Co., Ltd. for providing research resources and support.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, and no additional ethics approval is required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: The global economic recession and public fiscal contraction constitute a core governance paradox: economic downturns call for a lenient regulatory environment to stimulate market vitality, while plummeting fiscal revenues compel governments to intensify regulatory enforcement to expand the tax base and penalty collections. Drawing on the "Three-Level Prisoner's Decision Trap" (PDP) theoretical framework, this paper systematically analyzes the evolutionary mechanisms of government regulatory enforcement behavior driven by fiscal pressure in the context of the global economic recession. The study finds that economic recessions push governments into a dual prisoner's dilemma of "regulatory intensification" and "fiscal revenue expansion" through a threefold transmission pathway: "fiscal revenue contraction—rigid public expenditure—debt constraint hardening." At the micro level, local governments are forced to adopt short-sighted "penalty-driven revenue" strategies under survival-level fiscal pressure, falling into a "poverty decision trap." At the meso level, institutional fiscal decentralization imbalances and path dependence lock group decision-making into a "penalty economy" model, forming an "indigence decision trap." At the macro level, non-cooperative games among multiple actors trigger a "race-to-the-bottom" regulatory competition and trade protectionism, culminating in a "prisoner's decision trap." Using the U.S. federal debt ceiling crises and government shutdowns, alongside China's local government fiscal dilemmas and abnormal growth in penalty revenues, as representative case studies, this paper reveals how fiscal pressure progressively evolves through decision traps, ultimately undermining the rule-of-law business environment and long-term economic growth potential. The research provides a new theoretical perspective for understanding government behavior during economic recessions and offers policy recommendations for public finance reform and regulatory governance optimization.

title: The Solution of the Hesselager-Norberg Equation as a Path Integral
affiliations: Polytechnic University of Valencia

detail.title: The Solution of the Hesselager-Norberg Equation as a Path Integral
detail.abstract: The Hesselager-Norberg (1996) integral equation governs the state-wise probability distributions of the present value of a life insurance contract. Norberg (2005) derived its differential form by direct backward conditioning, located the points of non-smoothness that delimit its validity, and decomposed the solution by the number of transitions. This note writes that decomposition out explicitly. Read as a fixed-point equation, the integral system generates a Neumann series whose n-th term, once the recursion is unfolded, is an ordered integral over the jump times and a sum over the state chains, with the path density and the value functional displayed: a path integral, and the Feynman-Kac representation of the solution written for the distribution function rather than for the expected present value. That representation is shown to satisfy the composition law across an arbitrary intermediate time and to return, in the infinitesimal limit, the one-step factorisation from which the backward construction departs.

title: Improving India's Startup Financing Ecosystem: Grants vs. Equity Funding, A Quantitative-Comparative Analysis

detail.title: Improving India's Startup Financing Ecosystem: Grants vs. Equity Funding, A Quantitative-Comparative Analysis
detail.abstract: India's startup ecosystem, the world's third-largest with over 154,000 DPIIT-recognised startups and USD 150 billion in cumulative investment (FY2014-mid-2024), is underpinned by three principal public financing mechanisms: the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS), the Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS), and the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS). This paper examines whether grant-based or equity-based financing mechanisms more effectively support startup growth and survival across developmental stages. Employing a quantitative-comparative methodology, including cross-country OLS regression using corrected, source-verified data (N=20, R²=0.761, p<0.001), descriptive statistics, multi-dimensional benchmarking using author-constructed composite indices with explicit sub-component methodology, and feasibility-impact matrices, the paper finds that a 1 percentage-point increase in public innovation funding as a share of GDP is associated with a 1.36 percentage-point improvement in five-year startup survival rates (β₁=136.08, SE=17.96). Cross-country survival rates are drawn from OECD DynEmp3 (2025), World Bank Enterprise Surveys (2023), and national statistical sources. India's observed survival rate of 10% is below the OLS predicted value of approximately 17% given its current funding intensity of 0.08% of GDP, interpreted alongside the multi-dimensional benchmarking evidence as indicative of instrument design deficiencies rather than a quantum funding shortfall. Three policy recommendations are advanced: mandatory FFS transparency with performance-based capital allocation, the introduction of IIA-modelled repayable grants, and the establishment of deep-tech sub-funds with investment mandates of 12 to 15 years.

title: Pyxthreg: High-Performance Panel Threshold Regression in Python with Stata-Verified Conformity
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Pyxthreg: High-Performance Panel Threshold Regression in Python with Stata-Verified Conformity
detail.abstract: pyxthreg is a Python package for estimating fixed-effects panel threshold regression models of the kind proposed by Hansen (1999), the same model implemented for Stata by xthreg (Wang 2015). The package covers the full estimation pipeline described in Hansen (1999): a sequential grid search for one or more thresholds with Hansen's asymptotic refinement, a residual (wild) bootstrap test for the existence of each threshold that sidesteps the Davies (1977) nuisance-parameter problem, and likelihood-ratio-inversion confidence intervals for the threshold locations (Hansen 2000), together with classical and entity-cluster-robust inference, two-way (entity and time) fixed effects with no direct Stata equivalent, and an automatic sequential procedure for selecting the number of thresholds. Every estimation kernel is just-in-time-compiled with Numba (Lam et al. 2015) and an analytic incremental search algorithm removes the sample-size factor from the per-candidate cost of the threshold search, together yielding point estimates, standard errors, R 2 decompositions, and the true (non-bootstrap) F-statistic that match a live licensed run of Stata 17 on Hansen's own reference data set to four to six significant figures, and, in a dated, scripted, reproducible comparison (both the Stata and Python timing scripts are committed with the paper's replication material), completed the identical specification roughly 56 times faster, alongside a reproducible Python-only timing script bundled with the paper that substantiates the same order of magnitude on the package's own data, with no Stata installation required. This paper documents the econometric model and its Python implementation, derives the linear-algebra identities behind the fast search engine, reports the full empirical conformity and performance comparison against Stata, and works through the package's public interface with reproducible examples on data bundled with the package. One genuine, unresolved discrepancy between pyxthreg and Stata-in the simulated bootstrap critical values for the threshold-effect test, not in any point estimate-is reported and discussed rather than concealed.

title: Impact of RBI's Interest Rate Hike Cycle (2022-2024) on Term Deposit Mobilisation, Depositor Behaviour, and Systemic Liquidity in Scheduled Commercial Banks in India

detail.title: Impact of RBI's Interest Rate Hike Cycle (2022-2024) on Term Deposit Mobilisation, Depositor Behaviour, and Systemic Liquidity in Scheduled Commercial Banks in India
detail.abstract: This study examines how the Reserve Bank of India's rate hike cycle of 2022-24-a total increase of 250 basis points across six decisions from May 2022 to February 2023-affected term deposits, depositor behaviour, and overall banking system liquidity across eleven Indian scheduled commercial banks. The study tests four hypotheses using annual data for five public sector banks, five private sector banks, and one small finance bank, covering financial years 2021-22 through 2023-24. Four main findings emerge. First, the cost of accepting deposits rose significantly across all banks, with an average increase of 121 basis points. Second, CASA ratios-the share of deposits held in current and savings accounts-fell significantly from a sample average of 44.70 percent to 39.08 percent, as depositors moved their money into higher-earning fixed deposits. Third, nine of eleven banks simultaneously saw their CASA ratio fall and their credit-deposit ratio rise, pointing to system-wide funding pressure. Fourth, private sector banks lost CASA at nearly double the rate of public sector banks, which is consistent with their more financially aware, rate-sensitive customer base. A statistical regression model explains 66.9 percent of the variation in CASA ratios across the sample, with the cost of deposits emerging as the strongest explanatory factor. These findings are the first systematic banklevel examination of how India's deposit market responded to this rate cycle under the post-2019 External Benchmark Rate system.

title: Methodology of Pyxthreg: Complete Econometric Derivation and Linear Algebra of the Estimator, the Search Algorithm, and the Fast Incremental Engine
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Methodology of Pyxthreg: Complete Econometric Derivation and Linear Algebra of the Estimator, the Search Algorithm, and the Fast Incremental Engine
detail.abstract: This note is the exhaustive econometric and algebraic reference for pyxthreg, a Python implementation of Hansen’s (1999, 2000) panel threshold regression model. Rather than restating generic threshold-regression theory in the abstract, every assumption, lemma, and theorem below is derived from first principles in the exact notation and array layout the package uses internally, and is mapped to the precise source file and function that implements it, so that the mathematics and the code can be read side by side. The note covers the fixed-effects structural model and the projection algebra that eliminates entity and time effects; ordinary least squares estimation at a fixed threshold vector and the concentrated sum-of-squared-residuals identity; Hansen’s sequential search and refinement procedure for multiple thresholds; the Davies-problem test for the existence of a threshold and the heteroskedasticity-consistent wild residual bootstrap that operationalizes it; classical and cluster-robust standard errors; confidence intervals for the thresholds obtained by inverting Hansen’s (2000) likelihood-ratio statistic; and, in its most detailed section, the complete linear algebra and proofs behind the package’s fast incremental search engine, including the theorems that eliminate the need to rebuild the design matrix at every grid point. A final section documents four bugs found and fixed during the audit underlying this note, and one open item, each stated as a precise violation of a formula derived earlier rather than as a code diff.

title: pyxthreg User Guide : Panel Threshold Regression in Python (Hansen, 1999) -Complete Reference
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: pyxthreg User Guide : Panel Threshold Regression in Python (Hansen, 1999) -Complete Reference

contentType.other: pyxthreg User Guide for open source Software

detail.abstract: This document is the complete practical reference for pyxthreg, a Python re-implementation of Stata's xthreg command (Wang, 2015) for Hansen's (1999) fixed-effects panel threshold model. It documents every public class and method, every .fit() parameter and its exact behavior, the full results dictionary, the structure of .summary() output, the diagnostic plots, and the LaTeX/Stargazer export utilities, with copy-pasteable worked examples on the package's bundled datasets. A dedicated section reports conformity checks against a live, licensed Stata 17 run on Hansen's (1999) original dataset, including the one confirmed remaining discrepancy in bootstrap critical values, and a scripted, dated performance comparison. This guide is a companion to the separate methodology note, which derives the underlying estimator from first principles; here the focus is exclusively on how to use the package correctly.

title: Correlation-Gated Risk Budgeting for Equity Factor Portfolios

detail.title: Correlation-Gated Risk Budgeting for Equity Factor Portfolios

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, patients, animals, or the collection of personally identifiable information. The research was conducted using publicly available and/or computational datasets; therefore, ethics committee approval and informed consent were not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.
declarations.clinicalTrialRegistration: Not applicable. This study is not a clinical trial and did not involve any clinical intervention or patient recruitment.

detail.abstract: This paper studies whether a transparent correlation signal can improve the tail behavior of diversified equity-factor portfolios without relying on return forecasts, crisis labels, or a fitted regime-switching model. I propose Correlation-Gated Risk Budgeting (CGRB), a two-layer rule. The inner layer forms a long-only, capped minimum-variance combination of the Fama-French market, size, value, profitability, and investment factor sleeves using a Ledoit-Wolf covariance estimate. The outer layer reduces aggregate factor exposure when the mean pairwise correlation over the most recent 12 months rises relative to its 60-month reference. The rule is evaluated in a strictly rolling monthly experiment from July 1968 through August 2022, using only information available at each rebalance and charging 20 basis points per unit of one-way turnover. Over 650 out-of-sample months, CGRB earns a 6.80% compound annual growth rate with 2.43% annualized volatility, a 0.923 excess-return Sharpe ratio, a-4.20% maximum drawdown, and a 1.618 Calmar ratio. A static 70% minimum-variance portfolio has nearly identical return and Sharpe ratio but a deeper-4.78% drawdown and a 1.427 Calmar ratio. Relative to the unthrottled minimum-variance portfolio, CGRB reduces 5% expected shortfall by 0.585 percentage points per month and maximum drawdown by 2.735 percentage points; moving-block bootstrap intervals exclude zero for both differences. The evidence supports a narrow conclusion: correlation gating is more useful as a drawdown-control overlay than as a source of mean return or conventional alpha.

title: An Artificial Intelligence-integrated Building Information Modeling System for Automating the Building Permit Process
affiliations: Obafemi Awolowo University,  and Obafemi Awolowo University

detail.title: An Artificial Intelligence-integrated Building Information Modeling System for Automating the Building Permit Process
detail.abstract: The integration of BIM and AI will enable the implementation of automatic compliance-checking systems for building codes. It will enhance the precision, dependability, and efficacy of evaluating adherence to building requirements during the building permit procedure. Nonetheless, the possibility of using BIM and AI technologies in the automated building permit procedure remains unexamined. This study creates an AI-integrated BIM system to automate the building permission procedure. An AI-integrated BIM building permit system was built into an algorithm and a userinterface dashboard. The algorithm and dashboard were created to provide explicit guidelines for validating building information models of a design versus building requirements with an artificial intelligence technology. The AI-integrated BIM system for automating the building permit procedure was evaluated through a case study of a hypothetical construction project produced with BIM and assessed for compliance with building rules using an AI tool. The case study findings illustrated the system's capacity to comprehend building regulatory regulations, upload BIM files, and provide a compliance report based on the given criteria. The study finds that the technology facilitates a more efficient construction permit process and enhances future methods for obtaining permits.

title: The Boundary Illusion: Total Dynamic System Ontology and the Collapse of System Separation in Financial Markets

detail.title: The Boundary Illusion: Total Dynamic System Ontology and the Collapse of System Separation in Financial Markets
detail.abstract: Total Dynamic System Ontology (TDSO) is developed as a unified formal structure binding three parts into a single product: a contracting and expanding space, governed by orthogonality dynamics and the net rate at which manifold objects form and decay; the dynamics of a general object along its path, expressed through a nested cascade of coupling operators; and an ontology of continuous co-determination, in which the observer is embedded in the field it observes and every system boundary is a property of observation rather than of the market itself. It is to be recognized that coupling, under this construction, is not an exception between select factors but the continuous, structural default across all dimensions, objects, and systems. Applied to financial markets, the framework yields non-Gaussianity as a structural consequence. Existing mechanism-specific findings are proposed as special cases of a single coupled field, containing the Gaussian world. By dissolving the classification of endogenous and exogenous, it is to be expressly noted that no unexplainable change exists in the market — we simply fail to model reality as it is. Several formal components of the framework remain open and are marked as such; the contribution advanced here is the unification thesis and the architecture that carries it.

title: After the Unipolar Moment War, Currency and the Architecture of a New World Order: Russia, Iran, the Renminbi, Canada and Europe in an Age of Strategic Realignment
affiliations: Szymon Zephan Capital (SZC Group)

detail.title: After the Unipolar Moment War, Currency and the Architecture of a New World Order: Russia, Iran, the Renminbi, Canada and Europe in an Age of Strategic Realignment

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Managing Partner at SZC Group
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: SZC Group

detail.abstract: The unipolar moment did not end in a single diplomatic rupture. It eroded through war, sanctions, industrial policy, energy insecurity, payment-system adaptation and the diffusion of strategic capacity. This paper uses the Russia-Ukraine and Israel-Iran wars as distinct but connected stress tests of the emerging order. It evaluates military endurance, fiscal and industrial mobilization, energy and maritime transmission, sanctions adaptation, alliance cohesion and the weakening credibility of institutions that cannot consistently enforce their own rules. The monetary analysis separates reserve currency, invoicing currency, payment rail, funding market and political symbol. The renminbi is advancing most clearly in trade settlement and infrastructure, while capital controls, limited safe assets and institutional opacity still constrain reserve substitution. The dollar therefore faces diversification and network fragmentation rather than imminent displacement; the euro possesses greater financial depth but remains limited by incomplete fiscal and capital-market union. Canada is treated as a highly integrated United States partner that must preserve continental access while building strategic options through Europe, Asia, critical minerals, energy, defence production and trade infrastructure. Europe is assessed as a regulatory and economic pole whose security dependence, fiscal fragmentation and divergent national interests complicate strategic autonomy, including engagement by Spain and Italy with Iran amid wider European sanctions and security concerns. The paper develops four 2030 scenarios and a decision framework for governments, firms and investors. It concludes that the new order is not stable multipolarity. It is constrained interdependence: military blocs, selective economic separation and overlapping monetary networks operating inside a still-global financial and trading system.

title: Used Vehicle Price Differences in the Four Corners Area
affiliations: , affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Used Vehicle Price Differences in the Four Corners Area
detail.abstract: This study examines the factors that influence used vehicle pricing throughout the Four Corners region of New Mexico, Colorado, Arizona, and Utah. The purpose of the research was to determine why similar vehicles often have significantly different prices depending on whether they are sold by a dealership or a private seller. The project applies several core microeconomic concepts, including supply and demand, consumer choice theory, market competition, price elasticity of demand, information asymmetry, and value-added services. Vehicle information was collected from Don Reeves Auto Center, competing dealerships, Facebook Marketplace, Kelley Blue Book, and Edmunds. Vehicles were compared based on year, make, model, mileage, asking price, condition, financing availability, warranty coverage, and seller type. The analysis found that dealership vehicles generally carry higher asking prices because dealerships provide additional value through inspections, vehicle reconditioning, financing options, warranties, vehicle history reports, and customer support. These services reduce consumer risk and increase buyer confidence, creating a higher perceived value than many private-party transactions. Overall, the study demonstrates that used vehicle prices are determined by much more than mileage or age and are influenced by numerous economic factors that shape both consumer demand and market equilibrium.

title: The Theory of Cornered Rational Choice: Re-Engineering Labor Supply and Exit Power under Subsistence Constraints

detail.title: The Theory of Cornered Rational Choice: Re-Engineering Labor Supply and Exit Power under Subsistence Constraints
detail.abstract: Standard labor market models assume that workers exercise frictionless mobility when subjected to declining real wages or substandard working conditions. However, in low-skilled, precarious labor markets, empirical reality frequently displays a paradox: vulnerable workers often supply more labor hours in response to wage cuts. This paper formalizes the Theory of Cornered Rational Choice to resolve this behavioral anomaly. We establish that the primary, foundational driver of Giffen-style behavior-whether in product markets or labor supply-is the structural condition of being cornered (having zero accessible alternatives). We re-conceptualize the classical Giffen good as a Cornered Good to emphasize that such behavior is not a psychological anomaly, but the mathematical necessity of an actor trapped without an exit. In labor markets, when an actor is cornered near a binding subsistence budget constraint (B sub), leisure is stripped of its capacity to yield human well-being. The marginal utility of leisure collapses (M U l → 0) relative to the infinite marginal utility of survival consumption (M U c → ∞). Using a Slutsky decomposition, we prove that when access to alternatives is severed and exit cost becomes prohibitively high (C exit → ∞), labor supply exhibits a negative wage elasticity (∂Ls ∂w < 0). We show that secondary variables-such as unskilled human capital (S = 0) and singleemployer contract monoculture (n = 1)-are merely specific institutional mechanisms that execute this trap. The ultimate solution to restoring human agency is empowerment through skill conversion (S = 0 → S = 1), supported by structural safeguards that maintain accessible options.

title: Demographic Change and Private Consumption Expenditure in Germany: A Long-Term Projection
affiliations: and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Demographic Change and Private Consumption Expenditure in Germany: A Long-Term Projection
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the structure of private consumption in Germany in the very long run (until 2060). Using a large household data set, the official population forecast, and a long-term macroeconomic framework, we develop a comprehensive microsimulation model to study the implications of aging and of income growth for demand composition. Our results show that the structure of private demand in Germany will change dramatically in the long run, and that the income effect will be stronger than the population aging effect. These changes will have profound implications for economic policy, affecting both tax revenues, particularly VAT revenues, and the supply side of the economy. AI disclosure: The authors used OpenAI’s ChatGPT for language editing, improving clarity and consistency, and proofreading. It was not used to generate data, conduct econometric analyses, or derive empirical results. All output was reviewed and verified by the authors.

title: Nighttime Lights as a Proxy for Prefecture-level GDP: Evidence from Jiangxi, China (2012-2024)

detail.title: Nighttime Lights as a Proxy for Prefecture-level GDP: Evidence from Jiangxi, China (2012-2024)
detail.abstract: This paper constructs a prefecture-level panel for Jiangxi Province (11 cities, 2012-2024), linking NASA VIIRS Black Marble nighttime data to regional GDP from the Jiangxi Statistical Yearbook. Log-log correlations are strong (2024 cross-section Pearson r ≈ 0.98), and a pooled OLS with city and year fixed effects confirms a stable connection between nighttime light and regional GDP. Based on the increasing economic velocity, the K-means clustering analysis recognizes rapidly increasing areas like Ganzhou and Jiujiang. Using data from 2012 to 2023 as a training set and data from 2024 as a test set to run a holdout forecast, the result was RMSE ≈ 474 (100 million yuan) and MAPE ≈ 16.5%, varying by city. Nighttime light data is suitable for low-cost monitoring and regional economic ranking before the official GDP comes out, but it cannot replace statistical accounts.

title: Beyond Scarcity: Cultural, Psychological, and Existential Transformations in the Age of the Infinity Economy
affiliations: African Research Network (ARN)

detail.title: Beyond Scarcity: Cultural, Psychological, and Existential Transformations in the Age of the Infinity Economy
detail.abstract: The emergence of artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and generative digital infrastructures is transforming not only economic production but also the human condition itself. While existing scholarship has largely examined the technological and economic implications of AI, considerably less attention has been devoted to its cultural, psychological, and existential consequences. This article investigates how the transition toward an Infinity Economy-an economic paradigm characterized by increasingly generative, AI-enabled, and post-scarcity systems-reconfigures identity, work, education, creativity, social relationships, and human purpose. Drawing on interdisciplinary literature from economics, psychology, sociology, philosophy, futures studies, and AI ethics, the paper develops a conceptual framework for understanding how abundance reshapes human values and civilization. It argues that the principal challenge of post-scarcity societies is no longer the production of material wealth but the cultivation of meaning, creativity, ethical responsibility, and human flourishing within increasingly autonomous socio-technical systems. The article concludes that the success of the Infinity Economy will ultimately depend on humanity's capacity to redesign cultural institutions, educational systems, and social norms capable of supporting purposeful lives beyond the historical logic of scarcity.

title: Opening Up a Future for Ethnic Minorities: Lessons learned from the Conflict in the Chittagong Hill Tracts

detail.title: Opening Up a Future for Ethnic Minorities: Lessons learned from the Conflict in the Chittagong Hill Tracts
detail.abstract: As nation-states emerged in Asia, many ethnic groups that deliberately excluded themselves from larger ethnic formations were absorbed into the state, losing not only their self-identity but also their culture and politics. The Chittagong Hill Tracts of Bangladesh are one such example. This study examines in detail how the Bangladeshi government constructed the narrative that "there are no indigenous peoples" within the context of the resistance movement of ethnic minorities in the Chittagong Hill Tracts, the acquisition of peace agreements, the challenges of the autonomy system, and its connection to international norms. It also examines past successes of autonomy systems for ethnic minorities and suggests what international norms are necessary for the future.

title: Buddhist Reform in Nineteenth-Century Chittagong and Its Historical Significance

detail.title: Buddhist Reform in Nineteenth-Century Chittagong and Its Historical Significance
detail.abstract: The nineteenth century in South Asia was a period of religious reform. While Hinduism and Islam underwent movements of scriptural return and social reform, similar transformations occurred among Buddhist communities in Chittagong, eastern Bengal. In this region, a transition took place from indigenous Lurli Buddhism to Theravada Buddhism originating in Arakan. Luri Buddhism was a syncretic religious practice that incorporated elements of Hinduism, Islam, indigenous beliefs, and esoteric Buddhism. This paper reexamines Luri Buddhism, which has often been regarded as a deviation from Buddhist orthodoxy, and reinterprets the reform not merely as doctrinal purification, but as a process of religious boundary formation under colonial rule. The study first outlines the broader transformation of Buddhism in Bengal, then analyzes the Agar Tara texts, and finally examines the social significance of the nineteenth-century reform.

title: Fortunate Sons: Elite Political Selection in American History
affiliations: Boston University - Department of Economics, Stanford University, University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - Department of Political Science and Stanford University

detail.title: Fortunate Sons: Elite Political Selection in American History
detail.abstract:
We trace the family origins of Members of Congress (MC) born between 1830 and 1950, linking each MC, their parents, and their brothers to the complete-count censuses. Future MCs have always been economic outliers. By 1940, close to 60 percent of MCs aged 18--40 held a college degree, against under 5 percent of comparable young men outside Congress. In the 19th-century censuses, MCs as adults held roughly three times the wealth of demographically matched controls. They also come from economically elite families: their fathers earn more, attain more education, and hold more wealth. The brothers of future MCs sit between the population and the MCs themselves. Across the socioeconomic measures we compare, we calculate that roughly half of an MC's adult premium is shared with his brother and the other half is his own. Even as the American economy and political system have changed, the family background gap has widened over the last century and a half. Wealth, household servants, and four separate occupation-based scores all show the gap holding or growing across cohorts. We study four Progressive-Era reforms in a triple-difference design---women's suffrage, the secret ballot, direct primaries, and the direct election of senators---and none produce detectable shifts in who reaches Congress. Our results document a Congress drawn from the most fortunate families in American society in every cohort we observe.

Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

title: Robust Signal Maximization in Spillover Experiments
affiliations: University of California, Berkeley, Brown University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Robust Signal Maximization in Spillover Experiments
detail.abstract:
We study the optimal design and analysis of experiments for estimating spillover effects. Assuming a known (e.g., linear) exposure mapping, we characterize the treatment-assignment distribution and regression-based estimator that minimize worst-case asymptotic variance against a broad class of distributions of unobservables. The design problem yields an intuitive solution in which the planner trades off spillover signal strength against diffusion of spillover variation. The analysis problem yields a simple recentered instrumental variable estimator to best leverage this variation. This framework produces natural solutions in several benchmark cases -- such as clustered exposure-- and suggests computationally tractable approximations for general networks, including bipartite settings. We illustrate these new tools in semi-synthetic experiments based on two applications from development economics. Our approach yields large standard error reductions in both experiments, increasing effective sample sizes by 50–100% or more.

Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

title: The Sea Before the Storm: Freight Market Signals of U.S. Labor Market Stress

detail.title: The Sea Before the Storm: Freight Market Signals of U.S. Labor Market Stress
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether market-based indicators of global production and trade improve forecasts of U.S. labor market deterioration. Using monthly data from January 1990 to July 2026, we assess the predictive content of five maritime freight indicators spanning dry bulk, tanker, container, and cross-sector markets for cumulative changes in U.S. unemployment over horizons of three to twelve months. Direct multi-horizon regressions are combined with state-dependent specifications based on binary and continuous versions of the Sahm Rule. Robustness is evaluated using NBER businesscycle recession dates, oil-price controls, joint predictor regressions, a decomposition of level and momentum effects, and recursive pseudo-out-of-sample forecasts. The results reveal substantial heterogeneity in the macroeconomic information contained in freight markets. The Baltic Dry Index provides the most consistent predictive signal, particularly at medium-term horizons and during periods of labor market stress, whereas tanker, container, and composite indices exhibit limited systematic forecasting ability. Further analysis shows that elevated dry-bulk freight levels capture late-cycle conditions, while declining freight momentum provides a more immediate signal of weakening activity. The Baltic Dry Index also generates statistically significant out-ofsample improvements at six-and nine-month horizons. These findings identify global freight markets, and dry-bulk conditions in particular, as timely and state-dependent information variables for monitoring future U.S. labor market conditions.

title: Winning is Contagious: Social Learning and the Dynamics of Union Support
affiliations: Princeton University, University of Massachusetts Amherst, Columbia University, University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and London School of Economics

detail.title: Winning is Contagious: Social Learning and the Dynamics of Union Support
detail.abstract:
Union growth has historically happened in spurts. We combine union election data from 1961–2025 with a large-scale information experiment involving 9,000 low-wage workers to study the role of social learning in union growth. Observationally, close election wins cause future wins within state-industries. Experimentally, information about recent union wins increases union support and beliefs about co-worker support, with effects concentrated among workers with weak information environments and low baseline coworker support. In contrast, information about labor market tightness has little effect. Our results highlight social learning as a mechanism for union growth.

Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

title:
Why do Green Firms Pay Premiums for Green Commercial Real Estate? 
The Cost of Capital Channel
affiliations: National University of Singapore (NUS) - Department of Real Estate and Beijing Normal University - Zhuhai Campus

detail.title:
Why do Green Firms Pay Premiums for Green Commercial Real Estate? 
The Cost of Capital Channel
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether firms covered by major ESG raters pay acquisition premia for commercial real estate with green certifications. Using a dataset of over 260,000 North American CRE transactions, including 5,167 of those with green certifications, we find that ESG-covered firms pay approximately 7.7% to 8.7% higher prices for green assets than non-ESG firms. The premiums rise when climate-related concerns intensify, such as after the Paris Agreement, the BP Deepwater Horizon spill, and local natural disasters, consistent with firms accelerating transitions toward zero carbon goals. Our results further show that the premiums are driven by lower funding costs for ESG-covered firms rather than by differences in cash flow expectations.

title: Socio-Spatial Segregation in Indian Cities: Legal Violence and the Marginalization of Muslim Communities
affiliations: BML Munjal University

detail.title: Socio-Spatial Segregation in Indian Cities: Legal Violence and the Marginalization of Muslim Communities
detail.abstract: In India's booming urban sprawl, Muslim communities are being boxed into corners geographically, socially, and economically. This paper explores the socio-spatial segregation of Muslim communities in Indian megacities, focusing on how systemic discrimination in housing perpetuates cycles of exclusion, poverty, and marginalization. It critically examines the interaction between legal neglect, private discrimination, and social violence that reinforce spatial and social boundaries. Despite constitutional protections for equality, private actors and social practices often undermine these guarantees, leading to practices such as discriminatory enforcement, communal violence, and territorial stigmatization of Muslim neighborhoods. These processes result in deteriorating living conditions, declining property values, and increased police surveillance, reinforcing their marginalized status. The paper advocates for comprehensive legal reforms and urban policies that aim to foster inclusive housing, promote social justice, and address structural inequalities that sustain spatial segregation. By reimagining urban spaces as sites of inclusion, these reforms can challenge entrenched inequalities and facilitate better integration of Muslim communities into urban life.

title: Derivatives Clearing: A Comprehensive Guide — Risk Management, Regulation, and the Future of the Markets

detail.title: Derivatives Clearing: A Comprehensive Guide — Risk Management, Regulation, and the Future of the Markets
detail.abstract:
Client clearing is the arrangement through which market participants that are not direct members of a central counterparty (CCP) reach the clearing system through an intermediary. It is changing faster than any other part of the clearing chain, and this chapter examines that change from the seat of the clearing broker.

Five developments are taken up in turn: cross-product margining and the pursuit of portfolio optimization; the futurization of OTC derivatives and the practical limits of that convergence; automation and technology, including structural obstacles particular to the Japanese market; blockchain and distributed ledger technology, separating demonstrated use cases from expectation; and the direct clearing model, which uses the 2022 FTX proposal and its collapse to reappraise the clearing broker's function as a shock absorber, with a comparison to retail FX margin trading.

The chapter then turns to the intermediary itself: the lessons of the Archegos episode, the convergence of clearing brokers and prime brokers - its motivations, benefits, and risks - and the shift from a processor of margin toward a strategic partner supplying risk analytics, capital efficiency, and access. Two columns extend the analysis to the role of data and AI in financial platforms, and to the deepening convergence of cash and derivatives clearing.

The argument throughout is that proposals to remove the intermediary have underestimated what the intermediary absorbs, and that the role of the clearing broker is being redefined rather than removed.

title: On the Distribution of the Ratio of Quadratic Forms in Normal Random Variables
affiliations: University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management and Iowa State University

detail.title: On the Distribution of the Ratio of Quadratic Forms in Normal Random Variables
detail.abstract: In this paper, we provide explicit expressions for the distribution and the density of a ratio of quadratic forms in normal random variables, allowing a nonzero mean vector and a positive semidefinite denominator matrix. Our expressions are significantly simpler than the existing ones in the literature, converge geometrically, and come with computable truncation-error bounds, so that both quantities can be evaluated to any prescribed accuracy. When the denominator matrix is the identity, we obtain the density in both the central and the noncentral case, extending the central-case theory of Hillier (2001) to noncentral means, and the entire distribution can be evaluated on a grid at little additional cost. For a general positive semidefinite denominator matrix, the density is a finite combination of densities of linear combinations of chi-squared random variables evaluated at zero, with its value at a generalized eigenvalue of the pencil, where series representations break down, also in closed form. Finally, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the density to be continuous, an exact count of its derivatives at every point of the support, and its leading behavior at the endpoints of the support.

title: There is Such Thing as a Tame Bear: A Technical Reframing of AI Liability and the Applicability of the Wild-Animal Rule

detail.title: There is Such Thing as a Tame Bear: A Technical Reframing of AI Liability and the Applicability of the Wild-Animal Rule
detail.abstract: In Nondeterministic Torts: A Technical Approach to AI Liability, Trent S. Kannegieter argues that because today's in-production large language models (LLMs) are unavoidably nondeterministic, the harms they cause should sound in strict liability under ferae naturae, the wild-animal rule that applies to bears and other untameable animals. The Note's methodological commitment-that liability doctrine must begin from how the technology actually works-is a heads-up contribution to the AI-liability conversation. This Response argues, however, that the Note's doctrinal potential is undermined by its key technical premise. The engineering record, including sources the Note itself cites, establishes that LLMs are in fact fully deterministic. LLM-adjacent nondeterminism is a removable artifact introduced by non-LLM elements, not an inherent propensity of the model; this Response supplies a fine-grained formal proof of LLM determinism to give that point rigor. Because ferae naturae turns on an inherent propensity, the Note's regime loses its trigger once nondeterminism proves non-inherent. Keying liability to a removable property like nondeterminism allows technology to outpace doctrine. Holding to the Note's own methodological commitment, this Response identifies Lipschitz continuity as the appropriate replacement for determinism. This mathematical property appears novel to legal scholarship and cannot be outpaced by technological advance.

title: A Colonial Legacy: To What Extent do Postcolonial Borders Shape Conflicts in Africa? A Comparative Analysis of: Nigeria, Sudan and Rwanda
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Colonial Legacy: To What Extent do Postcolonial Borders Shape Conflicts in Africa? A Comparative Analysis of: Nigeria, Sudan and Rwanda
detail.abstract: This paper examines the enduring structural instability of post colonial states in Africa through arbitrarily drawn colonial borders that have created structural vulnerabilities in sovereign African nations. It applies John Stuart Mill's method of agreement, through a comparative analysis of Nigeria, Sudan and Rwanda using a postcolonial theory and constructivist framework. This study investigates how western state structures were imposed onto diverse fluid societies, reflecting structural differences of different African states and findings in difficult governance. Artificial borders create friction due to mismatched ethnicities and split nations. This makes post colonial governance harder for states, increasing institutional corruption and resource competition between ethnicities within the population. Findings indicate that while borders establish an initial baseline of friction, they act as the primary catalyst that turn spatial borders into active military conflicts within states. Borders are a vessel of structural vulnerability but don't guarantee war. Rather, conflict is triggered by domestic actions that exploit these lines for personal gains.

title: Company-owned Investment Bonds in UK Family Investment Companies: Accounting Basis, Micro-entity Eligibility and Tax Outcome
affiliations: Loxley Advisory Limited

detail.title: Company-owned Investment Bonds in UK Family Investment Companies: Accounting Basis, Micro-entity Eligibility and Tax Outcome

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is Founder of Loxley Advisory Limited and Managing Partner of Oscar Ip & Co Chartered Accountants, which provide UK tax, accounting and private-client advisory services, including advice concerning Family Investment Companies. The author has no financial interest in any investment bond provider, fund manager, platform or insurer discussed in this paper, and received no external funding or remuneration for preparing this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it did not involve human participants, personal data or identifiable case studies. All illustrations and scenarios are hypothetical and do not represent actual client engagements.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was undertaken independently by the author.

detail.abstract:
Purpose. Advisers sometimes assume that an investment bond held inside a Family Investment Company (FIC) delivers tax deferral, with growth rolling up untaxed and the eventual gain charged to corporation tax rather than income tax. That reasoning applies the wrong statutory framework to a corporate policyholder. Company-owned investment life insurance contracts are taxed as deemed creditor loan relationships under Corporation Tax Act 2009 Part 6 Chapter 11, under which the amounts brought into charge generally follow the company's valid accounting treatment. This paper examines how accounting basis, statutory eligibility, product type and extraction assumptions affect the outcome. It does not treat accounting basis as the sole determinant in every case.

 

Design and Methodology. The analysis applies Part 6 Chapter 11, HMRC guidance at IPTM3900 to IPTM3930, the micro-entity provisions in Companies Act 2006 sections 384A and 384B, and the measurement requirements of the September 2024 editions of FRS 102 and FRS 105, including the Periodic Review 2024 amendments effective for accounting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2026. Eight scenarios are modelled over twenty years for a UK additional-rate taxpayer investing £500,000. The model applies 45% to savings income in 2026/27 and the 47% rate legislated for 2027/28, then holds 47% constant for the remaining years as an explicit assumption. Scenario E uses a year-by-year schedule, a transaction-specific construction of CTA 2009 section 565 and same-period partial surrenders to fund corporation tax. A separate founder-funded sensitivity changes both the unused statutory credit and the director's loan. Corporate scenarios are also carried through a specified dividend-extraction layer so that founder cash can be compared with personal outcomes.

 

Findings. On the stated assumptions, a fair-value offshore bond inside the FIC returns £1,205,857 after twenty years, the same as the modelled fully taxable interest portfolio held by the company. Valid cost-based treatment of the same offshore bond returns £1,327,676. Holding the company, asset and extraction route constant, the accounting-basis difference is £121,819 within the company and £73,883 in founder cash. The personal-versus-corporate comparison cannot be reduced to a single rate effect: corporate annual taxation produces a £269,621 accumulation advantage before extraction, but the selected dividend extraction costs £277,755, leaving the personal annual-interest scenario £8,134 ahead. At an 8% gross return, the accounting-basis difference is £269,291 within the company and £163,325 after the selected extraction. The specified equity OEIC returns £1,419,640 within the company. In the self-funded onshore fair-value scenario, £88,958 of the final statutory amount treated as paid cannot be used in the modelled accounting period. A separate founder-funded sensitivity produces £131,068 of unused credit and a £679,631 director's loan; it is a different funding scenario, not an alternative statutory range.

 

Contribution. The loan relationship treatment of company-owned bonds, the accounting distinction, the absence of the individual 5% rule and the statutory tax-treated-as-paid mechanism are documented in provider technical literature, and no claim of first discovery is made. The contribution is a worked FIC-specific comparison carried through to founder cash, a decomposition of accumulation and extraction effects, and a year-by-year treatment of the onshore credit under a stated section 565 construction and funding convention. Searches undertaken to 3 August 2026 identified no directly on-point reported authority, official guidance or professional analysis addressing how the Companies Act 2006 section 384B investment-undertaking exclusion applies to a closely held FIC. That statement records the searches undertaken; it is not a claim to a systematic or exhaustive literature review.

title: Reconciling Rambus and Microsoft: Modeling Exclusion and Causation in Monopolization Cases

detail.title: Reconciling Rambus and Microsoft: Modeling Exclusion and Causation in Monopolization Cases
detail.abstract: Commentators often read Rambus Inc. v. FTC as imposing a heightened causation requirement in monopolization cases, an interpretation that is difficult to reconcile with United States v. Microsoft Corp. This article argues instead that the Rambus panel erred in analyzing exclusionary effects because it used the wrong model of competition. The panel treated a standard-setting organization's disclosure and licensing policies as merely constraining royalties after technology selection. In fact, those policies structured the conditions under which competing technologies were evaluated. The FTC found that, absent Rambus's deception, the organization would have either selected alternatives or required reasonable and nondiscriminatory licensing commitments. By evading those policies, Rambus deprived the organization's members of information needed to compare technologies and negotiate licenses before standardization, thereby distorting the terms on which technologies competed for inclusion. Although the panel retained this counterfactual framing, it mischaracterized the factual findings concerning how those policies shaped the selection process and concluded that the deception might have affected only royalties and not consideration of alternatives. Subsequent commentary has mistaken that discussion for a causation holding. Properly understood, Rambus concerns the threshold showing of anticompetitive effect, whereas Microsoft addresses the causal connection between exclusionary conduct and monopoly power. From that distinction, this article develops a framework for analyzing exclusionary conduct and methodological principles for managing evidentiary uncertainty, using counterfactuals, and applying institutional analysis in dynamic settings.

title: Rethinking the Gift in Diplomacy: Generative Relational Knowledge Emergence through Encounter

detail.title: Rethinking the Gift in Diplomacy: Generative Relational Knowledge Emergence through Encounter
detail.abstract: A gift asserts nothing that could be checked. It carries no proposition whose truth is at issue, and it discloses no procedure by which a content might be substantiated. It nonetheless does something that statements do poorly, and this paper asks what. The account offered is that a gift is composed by a reading of the recipient, that what crosses carries structure and no content, that the receiving party construes it under its own procedures, and that what it produces is deposited in the context against which its later construals are made. On this account a gift reaches the rule by which a party interprets only through what that party has already made of what arrived, so the alteration is mediated and is not an effect of the event. Three consequences are drawn, each with a simple dynamical illustration. A single crossing moves a state and returns, while a sustained practice moves the slower variable, which offers a reason for the repeated character of the practice. The interval before a return is of the order of the time the receiving system takes to relax, since a return offered sooner is composed largely of what the giver has just supplied and tells the giver little. And a gift that has gone wrong is poorly corrected by explaining it, because the explanation is construed against what the first construal deposited. A phase portrait of the slower variables is added and is stated for a class of coupled pairs in place of for any interpretation of them. It shows that whether such a pair admits one resting condition or several turns on the shape of one response, which the account does not determine, and that where two accumulations share one slower variable a given inequality between them rests at a larger value the higher that variable stands. The paper closes on the accountability that a channel asserting nothing cannot support.

title: An Anatomy of Injustice in the Emergence of Knowledge Among Heterogeneous Systems: A Preliminary Discussion in Generative Relational Terms of the Diplomatic Case

detail.title: An Anatomy of Injustice in the Emergence of Knowledge Among Heterogeneous Systems: A Preliminary Discussion in Generative Relational Terms of the Diplomatic Case
detail.abstract: A claim made by one party to another travels a course before it becomes anything the two hold in common. It is rendered into an event, construed at the far end by procedures the sending party does not run, registered or left unregistered in whatever description the parties share, admitted or refused at its source, and possibly carried onward by others. This paper takes that course as an anatomy and asks what may fail at each of its sites, distinguishing a failure of the operation from an alteration of the rule under which it is performed, the second of which escapes an inspection of what the site produced. Three results are reported. An assessment counting the occasions on which a claim appears to have been received as sent returns its highest values where the shared description has least capacity to hold a divergence. Reach obtained through intermediaries is purchased at the cost of fidelity, with no step on the route performed badly. And a complaint that a divergence went unregistered is unregistrable in the description whose incapacity it concerns. Two of the failures identified obtain where no party refuses anything and no collective resource for interpretation is deficient, which places them outside the categories the existing literature supplies; the absence of a perpetrator is taken from Fricker, and what is added is that the coarseness of a shared description follows from its being shared and requires no inequality. The final part treats the standing to raise a complaint and the forms of remedy available where the parties have accorded no third party the office of characterising their conduct. The account is stated in constraint form, and it proposes no further criterion of the kind its companion papers carry.

title: Diplomacy in a World of Heterogeneous Knowledge Systems: Exploring Generative Relational Systems Perspectives and Formal Models

detail.title: Diplomacy in a World of Heterogeneous Knowledge Systems: Exploring Generative Relational Systems Perspectives and Formal Models
detail.abstract: International arrangements are made among parties that differ in what counts, for each of them, as showing that a claim is so. This paper treats that difference as its object, taking a knowledge system to be the verification component of a normative order given dynamics of its own, and asks what two such parties can hold in common, what holding it costs, and what becomes of a claim in the passage between them. Four constructions are supplied. A joint description is represented as a common factor of the parties' dynamics, yielding the absence of a greatest such description and the result that an arrangement may cease to describe the parties' situation while every obligation it imposes continues to be performed.
